explain.say: It just bounces off! Now look at heat. When you warm a reaction, particles move faster. They collide more often, and more hits have enough energy. That is why food goes off faster in the heat. Why do you think your fridge keeps food fresh?

faq.a: Collision theory says particles react only when they collide with enough energy. Anything that makes successful collisions more frequent speeds up the reaction.
Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need to react. Collisions with less energy just bounce apart.

faq.q: Why does powder react faster than lumps?
faq.a: Powder has a much larger surface area, so many more particles are exposed and can be hit. More collisions per second means a faster reaction.
asks: How does surface area affect rate?

faq.q: How does temperature affect the rate of reaction?
faq.a: Higher temperature makes particles move faster, so they collide more often and more collisions have the activation energy. Both speed up the reaction.
asks: Why do reactions go faster when hot?

faq.q: How does concentration affect the rate?
faq.a: A higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so they collide more often and the reaction goes faster. For gases, higher pressure does the same.
asks: Why does stronger acid react faster?

facts: Reactions happen only when particles collide with at least the activation energy.
For many reactions, a 10 °C rise in temperature roughly doubles the rate.
